claims.statement: GOAI Agent Infra officially weights scene value, multi-agent collaboration, Skill engineering, engineering/runtime/security, and open-source contribution at 25/25/25/20/5.
The official track requires at least three different Agent roles and asks teams to map orchestration, decomposition, context passing, execution, and state tracking to AgentTeams.
Anthropic's official engineering guidance distinguishes workflows from agents and recommends starting with simple composable patterns before adding autonomy.

Anthropic's trustworthy-agent research frames self-directed plan/act/observe/adjust loops as increasing autonomy-related risk and emphasizes human control, alignment, security, transparency, and privacy.
The MCP tools specification treats tool annotations as untrusted unless the server is trusted and recommends that clients preserve a human ability to deny tool invocations.
The MCP authorization specification requires an OAuth 2.1-oriented authorization flow with resource/audience binding and forbids token passthrough.

A2A defines an interoperability model for independent opaque agents that supports capability discovery, modality negotiation, task collaboration, and multiple protocol bindings without sharing internal memory or tools.
The OpenAI Agents SDK documents traces and spans for model generations, tool calls, handoffs, guardrails, and custom events, including parent/child structure and sensitive-data controls.
OpenTelemetry's GenAI project defines development-stage semantic conventions for agent, workflow, plan, and tool-execution spans, including internal and remote agent invocations.

OpenAI's evaluation research argues that credible comparisons fix the harness, outcomes, tools, budget, and validity checks, because shortcutting, contamination, broken tasks, refusals, or sandbagging can distort scores.
The Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail? study reports 14 failure modes across specification/system design, inter-agent misalignment, and verification/termination categories.
Magentic-One presents an orchestrator that plans, tracks, and replans work across specialized agents and evaluates the system with repeatable benchmark controls and ablations.
τ-bench evaluates tool-agent-user interaction and pass^k reliability; its paper reports that strong-looking task results can remain unreliable across repeated trials.

ToolSandbox evaluates stateful tool execution with implicit state dependencies, user simulation, and intermediate/final milestones rather than treating each tool call as an isolated stateless function.
AgentDojo provides dynamic tool environments for indirect prompt-injection evaluation and reports security failures under adversarial task conditions.
The ACE paper treats context as an evolving playbook updated through generation, reflection, and curation, and reports task-quality, adaptation-latency, and rollout-cost gains on its own benchmarks.

LangGraph's official docs describe checkpointed persistence for pause/resume Human-in-the-loop, memory, time-travel debugging, and fault-tolerant recovery; its HITL middleware supports approve, edit, and reject decisions.
The Who&When failure-attribution study reports that identifying the responsible agent and pinpointing the failed step remain difficult, motivating explicit per-agent and per-step provenance.
A source-linked, hash-bound context envelope will reduce unsafe success and provenance UNKNOWN outcomes compared with unstructured handoffs, at a measurable token and latency cost.

The six-agent topology will improve structured conflict handling and independent verification over the single-agent topology on selected scenarios, but may lose on cost, tail latency, or coordination failures.

Structured memory compaction and retrieval can improve context recall under a fixed budget, but only a paired quality/cost/latency experiment can distinguish a real gain from retrieval overhead or stale-memory errors.
A provider-neutral evidence contract at MCP/tool boundaries and an opaque-agent boundary compatible with A2A can lower migration cost without weakening identity, tenant, or trace checks.
There is no checked-in evidence that ProofFlow's six-agent run improves quality, safety, cost, latency, or official score over deterministic or single-agent arms.
There is no checked-in ProofFlow A2A interoperability run or cross-framework conformance result.
There is no checked-in ProofFlow memory/context experiment showing a domain-quality gain after accounting for token, latency, stale-context, and security costs.
OpenTelemetry GenAI agent conventions are not evidence that ProofFlow currently emits compliant, complete, or stable agent traces.
Because the domain has a deterministic state machine, rule boundary, and calculation engine, a deterministic workflow may dominate dynamic agents on correctness, cost, latency, and auditability.

Every extra agent, handoff, memory write, and tool boundary adds coordination and attack surface; a six-agent result is not a safety improvement unless adversarial tests show no unsafe-success regression.
Results from public multi-agent benchmarks may not transfer to ProofFlow's synthetic employment-dispute contracts, so external benchmark wins cannot be used as ProofFlow claims.
Human approval and recovery waiting time can dominate end-to-end latency; mixing it into active compute would make a safer design look artificially slow or hide the real operational tradeoff.

sources.title: Agent Infra 新智基座 track details and review dimensions
limitations: This is the official rubric and requirement page, not evidence that any ProofFlow arm has run or earned points.

sources.title: Agent Infra 新智基座 participant handbook
limitations: The handbook describes submission requirements; it does not validate a local runtime, model result, or security claim.

sources.title: Building effective agents
limitations: This is vendor engineering guidance, not an independent benchmark and not a ProofFlow domain result.

sources.title: Trustworthy agents
limitations: The principles are a research framing, not a proof that any implementation satisfies them.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol 2025-06-18 server tools specification
limitations: A protocol recommendation does not prove that a client, gateway, or agent runtime enforces the boundary.

sources.title: Model Context Protocol 2025-06-18 authorization specification
limitations: The specification defines an authorization contract; deployment conformance and tenant isolation still require negative tests.

sources.title: Agent2Agent (A2A) Protocol Specification
limitations: The specification describes interoperable semantics; it is not a ProofFlow cross-runtime conformance run.

sources.title: OpenAI Agents SDK tracing documentation
limitations: The documented SDK trace model is not a claim that ProofFlow currently uses this SDK or emits complete traces.

sources.title: Semantic conventions for GenAI agent and framework spans
limitations: The page marks the conventions as Development and the repository is evolving; use it as a vocabulary reference, not stable compliance evidence.

sources.title: Trustworthy third-party evaluations foundations
limitations: This is evaluation methodology guidance and does not supply ProofFlow measurements or a winning score.

sources.title: Magentic-One: A Generalist Multi-Agent System for Solving Complex Tasks
limitations: The reported tasks, models, and benchmark results are not the ProofFlow domain and do not establish a six-agent benefit here.

sources.title: Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?
limitations: The study's frameworks, tasks, and annotations are external to ProofFlow; the taxonomy is a threat model, not a local failure count.

sources.title: τ-bench: A Benchmark for Tool-Agent-User Interaction in Real-World Domains
limitations: The simulated users, APIs, and domains differ from ProofFlow; pass^k is a useful reliability lens, not the current protocol's sole metric.

sources.title: ToolSandbox: A Stateful, Conversational, Interactive Environment for LLM Tool Use
limitations: The benchmark environment and milestones are not ProofFlow's contracts and do not prove a local tool-chain result.

sources.title: ToolSandbox official repository
limitations: The repository is a reference implementation and benchmark artifact, not an interoperability or security certification for ProofFlow.

sources.title: AgentDojo: A Dynamic Environment to Evaluate Prompt Injection Attacks and Defenses for LLM Agents
limitations: The tools, tasks, and attack model are not identical to ProofFlow; use it to design adversarial cases, not to import a security score.

sources.title: Agentic Context Engineering: Evolving Contexts for Self-Improving Language Models
limitations: The quality, latency, and cost gains are author-reported benchmark results; they do not establish a ProofFlow memory benefit or safe retention policy.

sources.title: LangChain Human-in-the-loop middleware
limitations: Framework documentation demonstrates a design pattern; it does not prove a human actually reviewed a ProofFlow run.

sources.title: LangGraph persistence documentation
limitations: Checkpointing provides a recovery primitive, not proof that side effects are idempotent or that retained memory is correct.

sources.title: LangGraph memory documentation
limitations: The documentation describes short- and long-term memory primitives; it does not show ProofFlow-specific recall, leakage, or cost measurements.

sources.title: Which Agent Causes Task Failures and When?
limitations: The reported attribution accuracy is from a separate dataset and should not be treated as a ProofFlow trace-quality measurement.
